# @phm-audit/dsh-action-guard
A deterministic pre-execution tool-call guard plugin for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`), registered throug
h the official **monotonic guard seam** (`ctx.tools.guard`).
> DeepSeek Harness follows an "everything is a plugin" architecture. This plugin fills one concrete
slot: a rules-based, operator-declared guard whose verdicts are reproducible and whose decisions are
les-based, operator-declared guard whose verdicts are reproducible and whose decisions are recorded.
Gate test artifact: 2009-frame deterministic command stream (2000 benign + 7 injected violations + d
eterminism/ledger/pathological-input checks, no RNG, no network) — **0 false positives on benign, al
l injected violations caught by the intended rule**, 12/12 vitest cases green (2026-10-13). Run: `ba
tions caught by the intended rule**, 12/12 vitest cases green (2026-10-13). Run: `bash run_demo.sh`.
## TL;DR — the four facts
- **Who it's for** — operators and teams running DeepSeek Harness where tool calls touch real system
s (shell, files, network, payments): they want tool-call policy they declared, not a model's judgmen

t call.
- **What problem it solves** — pre-execution, deterministic enforcement of an operator-decla
red tool-call policy at the official monotonic guard seam: unknown tools denied, forbidden keys/valu

es blocked, numeric bounds enforced — every verdict reproducible and recorded.
- **Key features** —
four deterministic rules (R-unknown / R-keys / R-equals / R-bounds) + fail-closed on internal error
+ a local JSONL decision ledger with chain ids; pure-function core (zero deps), cordis wrapper smoke

-tested against the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` package.
- **Current results** — 12/12 vitest
green; 2009-frame gate: FP=0 on 2000 benign commands, 7/7 injected violations caught by the intende
d rule; 3/3 end-to-end smoke through the real pipeline; parent methodology (PHM) validated on the Ag
entDojo official benchmark (v2.2 re-run: no ASR/FP events, fix-cycle 16→1→0 published).
End-to-end smoke: the Cordis wrapper is additionally verified against the **published npm packages**
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` + `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 0.0.1-rc.1 (2026-10-13) — loaded the co
rdis way (`ctx.plugin`, `static inject` resolved), a real tool registered, and a real `execute()` ca
ll to a non-allowlisted tool **denied with the expected R-unknown reason through the actual pipeline
** (3/3 smoke cases). Version-pinned smoke: the harness is under active development; re-run `npx vit
est run tests/smoke.harness.spec.ts` against your deployed version.
## What it checks (all operator-declared, all deterministic)

- **R-unknown** — tool must be in the declared allowlist
- **R-keys** — forbidden parameter keys per

tool
- **R-equals** — denied parameter values per tool
- **R-bounds** — numeric parameter bounds pe

r tool (inclusive)
- **Fail-closed** — an internal evaluation error denies with a distinctive reason

(a broken guard can never silently become a hole)
- **Decision ledger** — every verdict appended to
a local JSONL ledger with a chain id (correlation artifact for incident forensics; FNV-based chain
id, not a tamper-proofing guarantee)
## Method lineage — PHM
This plugin is the harness-native expression of the **PHM deterministic-verification methodology** (
gate-first, evidence-first), whose parent project agent-action-verifier is validated on the **AgentD
ojo official benchmark with a real LLM in the loop** (no ASR/FP events in the v2.2 re-run, FP fix-cy
cle 16 → 1 → 0 published, all artifacts open with SHA-256 chains, third-party thread engagement on r
→ 1 → 0 published, all artifacts open with SHA-256 chains, third-party thread engagement on record).
What that lineage means concretely, versus the (crowded, 155-plugin) Security & Permissions category
hat that lineage means concretely, versus the (crowded, 155-plugin) Security & Permissions category:
1. **Official third-party benchmark lineage** — the parent method is measured on AgentDojo, not only
on self-built samples (verified 2026-10-13 across a 10-repo sample of direct competitors: none cite
s an industry-standard benchmark; the closest, dsh-defend, uses a self-built 105-sample red-team set

).
2. **Cross-domain deployment record** — the same gate criteria (benign FP=0 / injected FN=0 / det
erministic repeats / fail-closed / audit ledger) run in robot (Unitree official-URDF gate), traffic-
flow (845k-frame NGSIM), and SDK-contract lines — a method with a track record, not a one-off plugin

.
3. **Open, recomputable evidence** — every claim in this README has an on-disk artifact: gate coun
ts in `tests/`, smoke in `tests/smoke.harness.spec.ts` against published npm versions, SHA-256SUMS m
ests/`, smoke in `tests/smoke.harness.spec.ts` against published npm versions, SHA-256SUMS manifest.
The category being crowded is stated on purpose: this plugin's value is the evidence chain and the s
tandard-interface demonstration, not feature uniqueness.
## Channel facts (from the #9614 review — thanks @argszero)
Four properties of the guard seam that scope what this plugin's ledger and rules can claim, verified
against `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts` at master (`d743267388`):
1. **The ledger is a guard-layer record, not a complete decision record.** The guard runs only when
the pre-execute waterfall returned `allow` (and the user did not refuse an ask, and the call was not
cancelled upstream). Denials owned by other layers never enter the guard — a complete audit record
needs `tools/pre-execute` + `tools/post-execute` as writers. Our JSONL ledger describes exactly this

layer and nothing more.
2. **`R-unknown` is a *name* allowlist, not a *tool* allowlist.** `executio
n.name` can resolve to different registered definitions across scopes (scope registrations shadow in

herited entries). A same-named shadow preset is indistinguishable to the guard.
3. **PTC mode change
s the traffic shape.** Model-direct calls of native tool names are denied upstream (`UNKNOWN_TOOL`)
before the policy pipeline; nested sub-dispatches *do* reach the guard (inheriting `rootCallId`). Po
licies must therefore cover sub-dispatch argument shapes too, and the allowlist only sees what actua

lly arrives.
